correspondence.component_scope: Headward Pole Creek and Mahogany Creek setting
correspondence.finding: The selected eastern opening corresponds to the Pole Creek/Mahogany Creek corridor on the northern Black Rock Range side of Summit Lake. It proceeds west past the mapped South Fork Mahogany Creek junction. Original cartography then shows Mahogany Creek turning toward Summit Lake, while the selected line turns away northwest before reaching the lake. This supports the initial local setting, not a whole-object Mahogany Creek identity or a selected passage through Summit Lake.

correspondence.component_scope: Northwestern transfer from the Summit Lake drainage toward Sand and Virgin creeks
correspondence.finding: The selected route crosses the plain north of Summit Lake and continues northwest through low terrain, small wet areas and a partly mapped unnamed drainage before reaching the Sand/Virgin Creek setting. The original map does not show a continuous selected waterway out of the Mahogany Creek corridor across this interval. Curry and Melhorn's actually read abstract describes an ancient northward Mahogany valley and pluvial overflow, but says the Summit Lake basin has been closed under drier climates. It does not establish this selected connection as a present river route.

correspondence.component_scope: Sand Creek junction setting and Virgin Creek canyon corridor
correspondence.finding: After the unresolved transfer, the selected line reaches the mapped Sand Creek/Virgin Creek junction setting and follows Virgin Creek north through its canyon and pond/wetland patches. The western Virgin Creek headwater arm and the southwestern Sand Creek reach are lateral to this selected approach. The map establishes the Hell Creek junction from the west and the further northeast continuation beside the Idaho Canyon Range toward the Sagebrush Creek junction and Virgin Valley.

correspondence.component_scope: Virgin Valley transition to Thousand Creek and its eastward gorge
correspondence.finding: Overlapping original views show the selected route entering the Virgin Valley wetland/pond setting, turning northeast through the narrow gorge labeled Thousand Creek, then continuing east alongside the Highway 140 corridor. The map distinguishes the Sagebrush Creek approach and small water patches from the named downstream Thousand Creek corridor. The images do not support assigning an unshown reservoir name to every pond or extending the Virgin Creek label through the entire gorge and lake system.

correspondence.component_scope: Rincon Creek junction and Continental Lake passage
correspondence.finding: The eastward selected route follows the mapped Thousand Creek corridor to the Rincon Creek junction and the southwestern entry setting of Continental Lake. It then traverses the lake/wetland footprint toward its long northeastern extension and the mapped Pueblo Slough corridor. Rincon Creek is a tributary approach from the north, not the selected main opening. The lake passage is a distinct waterbody component rather than uniformly Thousand Creek.

correspondence.component_scope: Pueblo Slough across the state boundary to Tumtum Lake
correspondence.finding: The selected route corresponds to the Pueblo Slough channel, wetland and pool corridor northeast of Continental Lake, across the Highway 292 and Nevada–Oregon boundary settings, then north along the Sand Hills to Tumtum Lake. The original maps establish the Denio Creek, Van Horn Creek and Cottonwood/Dry Creek junction settings as lateral approaches. The selected passage reaches the mapped Tumtum Lake footprint; neither the slough nor that lake is renamed Trout Creek.

correspondence.component_scope: Tumtum Lake to Trout Creek selected transfer
correspondence.finding: North and northeast of Tumtum Lake, the original map depicts separate dashed channels, wetland patches and ditch-like features associated with the westward Trout Creek approach and its north-turning trunk. It does not establish the selected direct northward passage out of Tumtum Lake across this setting as a through-connection into that northern trunk. Nearby mapped water and the broad Alvord Valley setting are not substituted for this missing link. This does not assert that all flood or managed connections are absent.

correspondence.component_scope: Northern Trout Creek corridor and Alvord Lake setting
correspondence.finding: Beyond the unresolved Tumtum transfer, the selected northward line follows the mapped Trout Creek wetland/intermittent-channel corridor east of Fields Road, past the Horse Creek and Steens Creek approach settings, toward the southeastern and eastern margin of Alvord Lake. The maps distinguish that lake from the Borax Lake area to the southwest and the separately mapped Willow, Wildhorse, Miranda and Bone Creek drainage on the lake's western and northern sides. No selected passage through Borax Lake is established.

correspondence.component_scope: Northeastern intermittent drainage and actual terminal in Alvord Desert
correspondence.finding: From the Alvord Lake eastern/northeastern setting, the selected route turns northeast across the mapped intermittent drainage network toward the southern Alvord Desert margin and continues into the playa interior. The original map supports this generalized terminal setting and distinguishes the desert playa from Alvord Lake. It does not show a named channel continuing along the selected interior line, and it does not establish present overflow frequency or a uniform river name across the lake-to-playa interval. The retained endorheic class is consistent with the mapped inland playa setting, without asserting a precise natural mouth point.

correspondence.component_scope: Selected headward approach east/northeast of Ibatiba
correspondence.finding: The Ibatiba original places the selected upper approach along the valley east/northeast of the Ibatiba urban area, near the BR-262/São José de Meriti setting. It traces the westward approach into Ibatiba and separates the northern São José/Carangola side drainage and southern Santa Maria branch. The AGERH original names this connected upper corridor Rio Pardo. The first generalized model tip is not asserted to be the named river’s natural source.
correspondence.mapped_component_name: Rio Pardo corridor; exact spring or small initial-reach name unassigned

correspondence.component_scope: Ibatiba–Vargem Alegre–Iúna upper river
correspondence.finding: Overlapping Ibatiba and Muniz Freire originals depict the southwestward river leaving Ibatiba, its turn south through the Barra Grande/Boa Esperança and Vargem Alegre settings, and its continuation into Iúna. The western Rio Pardinho joins separately near the Iúna approach. The selected channel continues south past Iúna, Barra do Perdição and the Terra Corrida setting; Pardinho, Ribeirão Perdição and local side streams are not synonyms for the selected whole route.

correspondence.component_scope: Muniz Freire hydropower corridor and Pardo–Norte Esquerdo junction
correspondence.finding: The Muniz Freire original traces Pardo south from Terra Corrida through the narrow Alto Cachoeira/Usina Hidrelétrica Muniz Freire corridor. Its surface channel reaches the river arriving separately from the north/northeast on the Muniz Freire side, then continues southwest. AGERH’s hydrography and hydropower originals identify Pardo, the receiving Braço Norte Esquerdo and the Muniz Freire hydropower site on Pardo. This establishes the confined impounded/hydropower valley and surface-river continuation at corridor scale. The small reservoir is not assigned an independent hydronym, and no turbine tunnel or individual dam structure is asserted to coincide with the generalized selected line.
correspondence.mapped_component_name: Rio Pardo / Rio Braço Norte Esquerdo

correspondence.component_scope: Itaici and upper approach to São Simão
correspondence.finding: The Muniz Freire and Alegre originals continue the same river southwest past Santo Antônio da Floresta, Frei Bento and Guaribu to Itaici, then south through the Pilões/São Simão surroundings. They distinguish the separate western Araraí/Boa Vista tributary and eastern Amorim and São Simão tributary approaches. The AGERH original keeps this as Braço Norte Esquerdo, distinct from the parallel Braço Norte Direito farther west.

correspondence.component_scope: São Simão reservoir passage and southern continuation
correspondence.finding: Quinto’s original Figure 14, based on the 2012/2015 aerial-survey period, shows the through-going north–south river widening into the long southern reservoir with short side arms. Its mapped position and shape overlap the selected lower Itaici–Limeira corridor. Figure 1 gives the study setting; the author describes the São Simão reservoir in the accompanying primary research prose. The AGERH original locates São Simão on this arm, while the overlapping Alegre original traces the same valley onward south below the reservoir setting. The thesis’s broad use of Rio Itapemirim is not used to erase AGERH’s local Braço Norte Esquerdo naming. No present shoreline, operating level or precise dam alignment is inferred.
correspondence.mapped_component_name: São Simão reservoir setting on Rio Braço Norte Esquerdo

correspondence.component_scope: Santa Fé diversion setting and natural two-arm confluence
correspondence.finding: The Alegre original follows the selected eastern arm south past Limeira and Barra São Lourenço to the Barragem Santa Fé setting, then downstream on the surface river to the junction with the western arm. It separately maps the expanded western Francisco Gross (Antiga Santa Fé) reservoir on Braço Norte Direito; that western approach is not inserted into the selection. The independently authored public Santa Fé EIA describes a derivation on Esquerdo, a generation reservoir on Direito, their tunnel connection, residual-flow surface reaches and the powerhouse below their natural confluence. Only this normally acquired EIA’s prose is used: its referenced map pages are blank placeholders. The municipal original supplies the mapped natural-river connection, and AGERH independently identifies formation of Itapemirim at the two-arm junction.
correspondence.mapped_component_name: Rio Braço Norte Esquerdo / Rio Braço Norte Direito / Rio Itapemirim

correspondence.component_scope: Departamento–Rive–Pacotuba eastward corridor
correspondence.finding: The Alegre, Cachoeiro and retained state originals overlap the river south through the Departamento/Fazenda Santa Fé setting, its turn east near the Rio Alegre junction, and continuation past Rive and the northern Jerônimo Monteiro surroundings. The mapped Itapemirim continues east through the Angico/Universo vicinity toward Pacotuba and the Floresta Nacional de Pacotuba. The western Alegre approach and southern local tributaries remain separate from the selected corridor.

correspondence.component_scope: Pacotuba–Coutinho and Castelo junction
correspondence.finding: The Cachoeiro original traces the eastward river through Pacotuba and Coutinho and the receiving junction with Rio Castelo arriving from the north. The river then bends south toward Cachoeiro de Itapemirim. AGERH’s original basin hydrography separately depicts Castelo and its contribution to Itapemirim, confirming that the selected east-to-south route stays on Itapemirim rather than following Castelo upstream.

correspondence.component_scope: Cachoeiro de Itapemirim, Ilha da Luz setting and Safra
correspondence.finding: The Cachoeiro and Itapemirim originals trace the continuous southward river through the Cachoeiro urban corridor and onward through the southern São Geraldo/União, Angola, Lambari and Tijuca settings to Safra and BR-101. AGERH’s hydropower map and table place Ilha da Luz on this same urban river. The source coverage supports that river/hydropower passage without inventing a separate lake crossing or a precise structure-to-model-vertex match.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower plain, Paineiras and Muqui do Norte junction
correspondence.finding: The Itapemirim original follows the river from Safra east and southeast across the lowland bends, past the Itapecoá/Paineiras and Ilha do Júlio surroundings toward Itapemirim. It separately maps the southern Rio Muqui do Norte approach through the Rio Muqui/Piabanha do Sul side of the plain and its downstream connection to the selected main river. AGERH’s original hydrography corroborates the Muqui contribution. Nearby southern lagoons and other coastal drains are outside the selected through-going line.

correspondence.component_scope: Itapemirim–Barra do Itapemirim estuary and actual Atlantic terminal
correspondence.finding: The Itapemirim original traces the terminal river past Itapemirim and its northward coastal turn, the wider estuarine reach and the Atlantic opening beside the Barra do Itapemirim/northern Marataízes setting. The retained state original prints Barra do Itapemirim here; AGERH’s hydrography marks the natural river mouth at the Atlantic. This is correspondence to the actual selected estuarine outlet setting, not a reassignment to nearby lagoons, beaches or towns. No exact modern bank, breakwater edge, sandbar or mouth-point agreement is claimed.

correspondence.component_scope: Western mountain opening and east-northeast foothill connector
correspondence.finding: Rincón Figure 1 and Apitz Figure 13 place the Aricuaisá drainage in the southern Sierra de Perijá and distinguish it from the more southerly Lora and Río del Norte drainage. Rodríguez and Galán Figure 10 maps the cave/foothill setting around the Aricuaisá system but does not extend clearly across the entire selected western opening. None of these actually read maps establishes the complete west-to-east-northeast selected opening into the mapped receiving corridor. Nearby cave locations, discovered Baracay labels and basin membership are not used to name or close this gap.
correspondence.correspondence: Regional headward setting only; full selected opening and connector remain unestablished.

correspondence.component_scope: Southeast-trending Aricuaisá approach across the piedmont and plain
correspondence.finding: Apitz Figure 13 separately labels the Aricuaisá and depicts its southeast-running approach from the Perijá foothills toward the common lowland trunk. Rincón Figure 1 overlaps this regional course. Urbani Figure 4.3 depicts the northern Aricuaisá approach distinctly from the southern Lora. This supports the middle selected approach as Aricuaisá, while leaving the more western selected opening unresolved.

correspondence.component_scope: Aricuaisá–Lora junction and Santa Ana receiving course
correspondence.finding: Apitz Figure 13 and Urbani Figure 4.3 depict a northern Aricuaisá approach meeting a separate Lora approach from the west/southwest, with Santa Ana continuing toward the lake. Urbani pp. 281–282 and the Figure 4.3 caption explicitly place the naming continuation after the Aricuaisá–Lora meeting. The selection comes down the northern approach and continues on the common receiver; the separate upstream Lora and Río del Norte are not renamed after it. The exact junction or name-transition vertex is not assigned.
correspondence.correspondence: Junction and receiving-course relationship read in original-publication maps and supporting prose.

correspondence.component_scope: Santa Ana lowland bends and northern tributary junction settings
correspondence.finding: Apitz Figure 13 carries the common trunk eastward and northeastward along the northern margin of the Juan Manuel wetland complex and separately shows the Santa Rosa and Negro/Tucuco approaches from the north. Rincón Figure 1 supplies overlapping lowland routing. The selected line remains on the receiving Santa Ana corridor rather than following any of those tributaries upstream. No intermediate reservoir or named open-lake crossing is shown on this selected fluvial interval; the broad wetland is its setting, not a whole-feature river alias.
correspondence.correspondence: Continuous regional receiving corridor, major tributary and wetland relationships read.

correspondence.component_scope: Lake-facing final reach and actual Lago de Maracaibo receiving setting
correspondence.finding: Rincón Figure 1 and Apitz Figure 13 visibly connect the Santa Ana lowland system to the western/southwestern shore of Lago de Maracaibo. Urbani Figure 4.3 and its caption independently show the lakeward outlet in historical cartography. The actual receiving waterbody is Lago de Maracaibo, not an open Caribbean or Gulf mouth inferred from the retained sea class. Rincón p. 23 discusses Caño Negro and Río Concepción in the lower wetland/outlet system; those prose names are preserved as limited branch context, not used as proven labels for the selected last segment. Exact current channel, bank or mouth-point agreement is outside this generalized correspondence.
correspondence.correspondence: Generalized outlet connection and receiving waterbody established; detailed distributary nomenclature not assigned.

correspondence.component_scope: Western opening and first connection
correspondence.finding: The opening lies in the mapped Tabocal/Jacutinga setting west of the Bahia frontier. The drawn watercourse continues east through the Cabeceira do Rio do Peixe setting into the frontier river corridor. This establishes geographic continuity without assigning one hydronym to the whole opening.
correspondence.correspondence: Positive original-map correspondence at generalized corridor/component scale.

correspondence.component_scope: Frontier and Buranhém settlement corridor
correspondence.finding: The mapped corridor continues from the frontier east through the Buranhém settlement area, receiving separate side streams and then turning northeast. The settlement label is distinguished from the downstream river labels.
correspondence.correspondence: Positive original-map correspondence at generalized corridor/component scale.

correspondence.component_scope: Alto Cariri northeast bend and eastward turn
correspondence.finding: Overlapping maps show the northward bend east of the Alto Cariri area and the turn east toward Eunápolis. Separate tributary junctions, including the Água Preta setting, join this continuous course; the Guaratinga sheet prints Rio Buranhém ou Peixe on the trunk.
correspondence.correspondence: Positive original-map correspondence at generalized corridor/component scale.

correspondence.component_scope: Middle course south of Eunápolis
correspondence.finding: The same corridor passes south of Eunápolis, crosses the BR-101 setting and continues east toward Vera Cruz, with the selected broad southward loop and return north shown in overlapping sheets.
correspondence.correspondence: Positive original-map correspondence at generalized corridor/component scale.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower bends and estuary approach
correspondence.finding: The lower course follows the mapped Vera Cruz/Vale Verde bends, turns east below the BR-367/Pindorama setting and broadens toward Porto Seguro. The Porto Seguro original again prints Rio Buranhém ou Peixe on this connected course.
correspondence.correspondence: Positive original-map correspondence at generalized corridor/component scale.

correspondence.component_scope: Lake/reservoir passages and lateral tributaries
correspondence.finding: The inspected selected corridor is depicted as a connected river course with tributary junctions and lower estuarine widening. No intervening named lake or reservoir passage is depicted. Lateral stream labels are not adopted as names for the selected whole.
correspondence.correspondence: Positive original-map correspondence at generalized corridor/component scale.

correspondence.component_scope: Actual terminal
correspondence.finding: The final mapped channel opens directly to the Atlantic between the Porto Seguro urban waterfront and the Arraial d’Ajuda/Aldeia Velha side. The selected terminal corresponds to that sea outlet, not an upstream junction or a separate coastal stream.
correspondence.correspondence: Positive original-map correspondence at generalized corridor/component scale.
